stable.label: ecosystem-surface-liquid-ci-pass
stable.note: The ecosystem remains the primary experience. The continuous open-surface water layer has independent Codehood and Foundation CI evidence, but deployed-browser/iPhone behavior is still unverified.

active_experience.current_change: replace visible open-surface falling-cell water with a continuous conservative free-surface heightfield solver that carries depth and momentum, couples to bodies, and drives erosion
approximations: surface_liquid is a 1D local-inertial shallow-water approximation over the open terrain surface, not full 2D CFD
enclosed cave water is not represented by the shallow-water field and remains outside this solver's verified scope
legacy fine/coarse water state is absorbed as a source/reservoir rather than displayed as the primary visible liquid
lava still uses the older material solver and has not yet been converted to a continuous viscous free-surface model
creature locomotion still contains legacy authored body drive

surface_liquid.representation: 1D local-inertial shallow-water free-surface approximation over open terrain

fluid_refinement.representation: 2D subcell water-volume field with pairwise conservative transfer and damped momentum proxy

active_objective: Exercise the deployed ecosystem on iPhone and verify that open water now forms continuous pools/streams rather than visible falling-cell liquid. If that is stable, convert lava separately to a viscous continuous free-surface model and then add depth-aware connected basins/cave water.
next_gate: LIVE_TESTED requires deployed-browser execution with surface_liquid active. DEVICE_TESTED requires the iPhone Safari run after that. CI_PASS alone is not sufficient.
invariants: Do not call surface_liquid full 2D CFD or full 3D physics
Continuous water rendering must derive from the simulated depth field
Open-water legacy cells are source/reservoir inputs, not the primary visible liquid
Erosion claims require authoritative terrain state changes
